This writ petition is filed declaring the action
 of Respondents in not considering the case of
the Petitioner for appointment and not allowing the Petitioner to un

sentences.text: dergo for training for the Post of Police Constable on the ground of pendency of criminal case as illegal and arbitrary
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: . A notification was issued on 28.11.2022 for recruitment of Police Constables by Respondent No.2.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
The Petitioner,
being eligible, applied and was selected for the post of Police Constable.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, he was not being sent for training on the premise that a criminal case is pending.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Hence, the present writ petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that a case in FIR.No.229 of 2021 dated 15.12.2021 under Sections 376(2)(N), 354-D(1), 354-C and 417 IPC has been registered against the Petitioner and his family members in connection with dispute between his elder brother and the complainant and in that context, Petitioner was arrayed as A.3 though no specific attributions were made in the charge sheet against the Petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: subsequently, both complainant and brother of the Petitioner get married with others separately.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, mere pendency of the criminal case cannot come in the way of Petitioner being sent for training for being appointed as Police Constable.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Government Pleader Sri S.Raju on instructions submits that it would be impermissible to appoint a person as a Police Constable even though he is facing a criminal case.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
In the present case, the nature of the criminal case against the Petitioner is with regard to the offences under Sections 376(2)(N),
354-D(1), 354-C and 417 IPC, and it is not advisable to send such persons for training.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for both the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 19 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is to be noted that criminal case cannot be an absolute bar for sending an individual selected for training and the Respondent- authorities are required to examine the nature of allegations against the Petitioner in the charge sheet and then take a conscious decision whether to send the person to training as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Avtar Singh v. Union of India and others (2016 Supreme (SC) 578).

opennyai_summary.facts:
. A notification was issued on 28.11.2022 for recruitment of Police Constables by Respondent No.2.
The Petitioner,
being eligible, applied and was selected for the post of Police Constable.
However, he was not being sent for training on the premise that a criminal case is pending.
opennyai_summary.19_December_2025__arguments:
Therefore, mere pendency of the criminal case cannot come in the way of Petitioner being sent for training for being appointed as Police Constable.
In the present case, the nature of the criminal case against the Petitioner is with regard to the offences under Sections 376(2)(N),
354-D(1), 354-C and 417 IPC, and it is not advisable to send such persons for training.
opennyai_summary.19_December_2025__ANALYSIS: It is to be noted that criminal case cannot be an absolute bar for sending an individual selected for training and the Respondent- authorities are required to examine the nature of allegations against the Petitioner in the charge sheet and then take a conscious decision whether to send the person to training as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Avtar Singh v. Union of India and others (2016 Supreme (SC) 578).

opennyai_summary.final__PREAMBLE:
Proceeding Sheet vs Unknown on 4 February, 2026
High Court Of Andhra Pradesh::At Amaravati Main Case No. Crl.A.No.68 of 2022
Proceeding Sheet Sl. Office Date Order
No. NOTE 10. 04.02.2026 KSR,J & AHHS,J
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice K.Suresh Reddy) I. A.No.1 / 2025 The present application is filed by the petitioner / appellant / A.1 under Section 430 (1) B.N.S.S. seeking his release on bail.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the offence took place in the year 2015, but the learned trial Judge awarded sentence by following the amended provision.
As such, learned counsel states that the sentence imposed on the appellant by the learned trial Judge is not proper.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application contending that similar application filed by the petitioner vide I.A.No.1/2022 was dismissed by order dt.
22.02.2022.
He further contended that as per the provisions of Section 376(2)(i) IPC, punishment was prescribed for 'LIFE', which shall mean remainder of LIFE, but not less than 10 years.
As such,
the learned trial Judge ought to have convicted the appellant under Section 376(2)(i) IPC in view of Section 42 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act).
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Be that as it may, the above aspect can be considered at the time of final hearing, but not at this stage.
As the petitioner / appellant / A.1 was convicted under Sections 363 & 344 IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act, this Court is not inclined to enlarge the petitioner / appellant / A.1 on bail at this stage.
Accordingly, this application is dismissed.
Post the appeal for hearing in usual course.
